column3: The Hebrew explicitly says “for yourself” with both chiseling the tablets and making the ark; BSB omits both expressions.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “in my hand” in the singular; BSB has plural “in my hands.”
The Hebrew calls them “the ten words”; BSB says “the Ten Commandments.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “there” with Aaron’s death and burial; BSB combines the location in one “where” clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with “until this day”; BSB expands this into “as they do to this day.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name and says He “was not willing” to destroy you; BSB uses His name once and says He “agreed not to destroy you.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists fearing the LORD and walking in His ways as parallel infinitives; BSB connects them as fearing Him “by walking” in His ways.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the heavens of the heavens”; BSB says “the highest heavens.”
The Hebrew uses the image of the fathers’ “seed”; BSB says “descendants.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the heart’s “foreskin” and uses singular “heart” and “neck”; BSB omits “foreskin” and has plural “hearts” and “necks.”
The Hebrew says God does not “lift faces”; BSB expresses this as “showing no partiality.”
The Hebrew says “bread”; BSB says “food.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to “these great and awesome things” without an explicit noun “wonders”; BSB supplies “wonders.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the seventy as souls or persons; BSB says “seventy in all” without a corresponding noun.
